metadata.concept_name: ZeroFizz Sugar-Free Carbonated Beverage - Jobs to be Done
metadata.product_name: ZeroFizz Sugar-Free Carbonated Beverage - Jobs to be Done
metadata.objective: Understand what jobs health-conscious adults 18-35 are trying to accomplish when they reach for a sugar-free carbonated beverage — functional jobs (power through the 2pm desk slump without another coffee, substitute for a beer at a rooftop bar, scratch the soda craving without a calorie hit), emotional jobs (feel indulgent without guilt, feel alert without jittery, feel like the kind of person who reads labels), and social jobs (have an adult-coded drink in hand while friends are doing Dry January, signal wellness alignment without preaching). Probe the pains driving switching — sweetener aftertaste fatigue, a TikTok creator calling out an ingredient, price creep, availability drops at their usual grocery. Elicit desired outcomes — clean energy, recognizable short-label ingredients, a flavor that doesn't get boring. Treat Coke Zero, Celsius, LaCroix, and Olipop as category alternatives respondents are hiring against.

turns.question: I'd love to hear about your experience with drinks lately — so think back to maybe the last week or two when you grabbed a sugar-free soda or fizzy drink instead of something else. What was going on at that moment, and what made you reach for that particular drink?
turns.response: Honestly, I don't reach for that stuff that often. But like, last week I was at work and had this afternoon slump around 3pm, and I just grabbed whatever was in the break room fridge. It happened to be one of those zero sugar sodas, so I went with it instead of just having coffee again.

turns.question: Why does having something other than coffee matter when that afternoon slump hits at work?
turns.response: I guess coffee gets old after a while, you know? Like if I've already had two cups by 2pm I don't want another one. Something carbonated just feels different, more refreshing I think. Plus the fizz kind of wakes you up in its own way.

turns.question: When you're picking between that zero sugar soda and coffee in the afternoon, what makes the fizz feel more refreshing than just having another cup?
turns.response: I think it's just the carbonation honestly. Like coffee's good but it's the same thing I already had this morning, you know? The fizz feels like it actually does something — it's more of a pick-me-up in a different way. Plus there's something about the bubbles that just feels sharper I guess, more refreshing on your mouth than just drinking something flat.
